newsitem.title: USA: Mediator somewhat more hopeful on American, pilots talks.
newsitem.headline: Mediator somewhat more hopeful on American, pilots talks.

text.p: Federal mediator Kenneth Hipp said on Friday that he was somewhat more encouraged by the negotiations between American Airlines and its pilots in their efforts to avert a strike threatened for midnight(0500 GMT Saturday).

But, reporting on the around-the-clock talks between the two sides, he said major issues remain and that American and the Allied Pilots Association were continuing to try to reconcile their differences.
Hipp said that while some progress had been made, "there are major points that have to be resolved between now and midnight."
He added that the mediators have not made any recommendation to President Clinton as to whether he should intervene to avert a strike and set up an emergency board to try to resolve the dispute.

Earlier, Allied Pilots Association President James Sovich told reporters that "we've had minor progress on some issues." But asked whether he thought a strike was likely, he said the position was "no different from what it was yesterday."
On Thursday he said "a strike was more likely than not."

A shutdown of American, the nation's No. 2 two airline, would disrupt travel plans for some 200,000 passengers on the carrier's 2,200 routes worldwide every day, as well as play havoc with mail and cargo shipments.
